commit.message:
fix(drilling): Drill, Bore and Thread take a start and an exit pick as the hole order

Drill, Bore and Thread (mill) cut their holes in the list order and
refused a start or exit pick as "not taken". The three kinds now answer
PickCapability::HoleOrder: the hole under the start pick is cut first,
the hole under the exit pick is cut last, and the holes between keep the
list order, rotated to the start hole (camcraft_motion::drilling::
hole_order). With no pick the hole list is unchanged, so every earlier
program is byte-identical.

Refused by name, never moved: a pick that is on no hole, a start and an
exit pick on one hole of a longer list, a pick on a Drill with cross
holes, and a pick on a lathe's axial Drill. The door (named_refusal)
refuses the first three; the generator checks again and owns the lathe
refusal.

The operation page draws typed First hole / Last hole rows for the three
kinds. MCP edit_operation sets the picks through EditOperationParams.

Fixes #3328

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(sinker): Sinker Burn and Sinker Side Burn take a start and an exit pick

A Sinker Burn reads a pick as an angle round its burn position. The
start pick is where the orbit starts; the exit pick is where the orbit
ends before it returns to the burn position and retracts. A circle keeps
its own vertices and makes one full turn; a vector orbit keeps its
directions and changes the order only. A Sinker Side Burn reads a pick
as an end of its side move: the burn position or the wall end.

An impossible pick is refused by name at the command door and at
generation: a pick without an orbit, a pick on the burn position, a
pick on no vector, an exit that the vector order cannot end on, a side
burn pick at the middle of the move. With no pick each generator calls
the earlier function, so every existing path is identical.

The Geometry tab of each kind has typed Start point and Exit point
groups. MCP edit_operation sets the picks through the shared field.

Fixes #3333

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(2d): the Face raster takes a start pick and an exit pick

The Face always started its raster at the corner that the generator
selected. The start pick now takes the corner of the face region nearest
to it: its edge row is cut first and the rows step to the far edge. The
exit pick names the side where the last row ends. A side that the row
count cannot reach from the start corner is refused by name. An exit pick
alone chooses the start corner that reaches it.

The rows never change: a pick only orders the facer's own band, so the
overrun, the holes law, the "Do not touch" law and the air entry read the
same rows. No pick is the automatic raster to the byte.

- motion: `face_raster` (the planning rule) and `face_picked` (the entry
  point); `face_over_kept` calls it with no pick.
- app: Face answers `PickCapability::Raster`; the picks are turned into
  the laid frame of an open boundary; a tilted (3+2) Face refuses a pick
  by name.
- mcp: the `edit_operation` schema names the Face rule.
- ui: the Face Geometry tab shows typed Start point and Exit point groups.

Fixes #3326

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.2 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(wire): a tangent arc lead-in and lead-out

Wire Contour takes an opt-in tangent arc lead (`lead_arc_radius`, mm)
next to the straight lead, which stays the default. The lead circle
touches the path at the seam on the waste side; a tangent straight from
the start hole and an arc enter the path in its own direction, and the
mirror leaves it. A radius not over the kerf offset, a hole inside the
lead circle and a lead nearer the profile than the kerf offset are
refused by name, and so is the arc lead beside an open run, tabs,
skims, a taper, a burnout, a 4-axis cut, an exit pick or a model's
profile. Project file (serde default), MCP field, UI row and the
camcraft-mcp skill row follow.

Refs #3937
Fixes #3991

fix(2d): the Face picks hold under a rotated work offset and a keep-out

Review of PR #3997, findings 1 and 2.

- A work offset with a Z rotation carries the geometry into the
  generator frame. `wcs_yaw::rotate_params` now carries each start and
  exit pick with it (`OpParams::path_picks_mut`, each kind that stores
  picks). The Face read the picks in the setup's frame against a rotated
  region, so the model pick (29, 19) took the wrong corner.
- The picks are judged again on the rows that each level cuts
  (`face_raster::Raster::held`). A hole or a "Do not touch" keep-out that
  takes the first or the last row is refused with the blocked pick named
  and marked. Before, the exit was accepted from the uncut row count and
  the cut ended on the other side.

Pinned by `a_rotated_work_offset_reads_the_picks_in_the_setup_frame`
(app) and
`a_keep_out_that_takes_a_terminal_row_refuses_the_blocked_pick_by_name`
(motion).

Refs #3326

commit.message:
ci(post-merge): skip the gate for docs-only and process-only commits

A push whose commit changes only site/, docs/, *.md or .claude/ (against its
first parent) now sets skip=true in the existing yield step with the notice
"no code changed - the previous run covers this code". Markdown under code
directories (crates/, xtask/), assets/, scripts/, build.rs, Cargo files and
.github/ always run the gate; workflow_dispatch always runs. The checkout
fetches two commits so the step can diff against the parent.

Fixes #4054
